transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
Russia is stepping up attacks on Ukraine's power grid ahead
of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi this week.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports the latest round
of airstrikes has left hundreds of thousands
of people without electricity.
>> The attacks are part of the Kremlin's strategy
to freeze Ukrainians and leave them in the dark this winter.
A regional military spokesperson said Ukraine's power company
DTEC is working to restore electricity,
but efforts are being hampered by constant Russian shelling.
Alexander Hanza said hospitals had been forced to switch
to diesel generators, and electric-powered public transport
had ground to a halt in the large eastern city of Nipro.
President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia
of seeking to apply maximum pressure ahead
of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi in the coming days by,
quote, "plunging the entire country into a blackout."
Russia began stepping up attacks
on Ukrainian energy infrastructure in late September.
It has targeted the sector every winter
since launching its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv.
>> After brutal losses for the Republican Party
in last week's midterm elections,
President Trump says he's open to working with Democrats.
But the staffing moves he's been making
would help suggest otherwise.
He's replacing Chief of Staff Susie Wiles
with her deputy, Stephen Miller, a hardliner
who's the architect of Trump's immigration policy.
Empirus Franco Ordonez has more.
>> It really is a wait-and-see moment.
I mean, Trump says he wants to work with Democrats,
but the appointment of Miller and other comments, too,
like posting a picture of a red MAGA hat saying Mr. Vito,
suggesting, for example, the ultimate fighting chief
to be the press secretary.
It all just sends a different message.
And just to put one more point on this,
even some Republicans have spoken out
about Miller's appointment
questioning whether Trump learned his lesson
after such devastating midterm losses.
You know, but, as we've learned,
Trump is going to do what Trump wants to do.
>> Empirus Franco Ordonez.
But today, Trump says he was only kidding
about appointing UFC CEO Dana White
to the press secretary job.
Investors on Wall Street are gearing up
for the latest inflation report that's due out this week.
Empirus Rafael Nam has more.
>> The U.S. is set to report
how much consumer prices rose in October
at a time when voters have said they're struggling
with the cost of living in the most recent midterm elections.
One thing to note is that there's not going to be
a comparison to a year ago because of a government shutdown
that prevented the Labor Department
from compiling the report in October last year.
But investors will be seeing how consumer prices fared
last month compared to September
to get a better gauge of how inflation is doing.
The report comes at a time when stock markets
are under pressure amid fears about the outlook for AI shares.
Rafael Nam, NPR News.
>> You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
A collection of red barns
sits inside the University of Maryland at College Park.
It's the campus farm,
and it's a remnant of the university's ag school
pass that's still in use today.
Ari Daniel has more.
First stop, cows.
>> I'm a dairy cattle person.
To me, cattle are beautiful.
>> Adele Terzillo chairs the Department of Animal
and Avian Sciences.
She says the students here, who largely go on to become vets,
get a very hands-on education.
Liliana Sunpar is a senior.
>> I actually had the experience
of helping to deliver a horse last spring.
>> This kind of learning makes her proud.
>> Yes, you can learn your chemistry,
but no one can teach you how to bottle-feed a lamb
unless you actually do it.
>> As a result of her studies here,
Sunpar says her idea of what it means to be an impactful vet
has expanded tenfold.
For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.
>> A drone delivered food to a hungry ape
at a chimp sanctuary in Florida this weekend
after he was cut off from his enclosure
by floodwaters from last week's heavy rains
when he decided not to follow his fellow chimps inside.
Save the Chimps in Fort Pierce CEO Paula Tavares says
Caleb missed a couple of meals.
>> When we became concerned that he was out
and not able to come in to get his fruits and vegetables,
that's when we send him some nourishment through the drone.
>> Now, the organization used a drone before
to feed a blind chimp.
I'm Janine Herbst,
and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Russia steps up strikes on Ukraine's power grid ahead of Abu Dhabi talks, leaving hundreds of thousands without electricity
Trump replaces Chief of Staff Susie Wiles with deputy Stephen Miller, a hardline immigration architect, after midterm losses
Trump says he was only kidding about appointing UFC CEO Dana White as press secretary
Investors await October consumer price inflation report amid stock market pressure over AI shares
University of Maryland's campus farm and animal science program provide hands-on training for future veterinarians
Drone delivers food to chimp Caleb at Florida sanctuary after floodwaters cut off his enclosure access
